### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The Picker's entire action region does not exist on a phone: Copy color, Reset color, Random color, Palettes, Extract palette and Open color input are in the dock on desktop and absent from the whole document on mobile.

**Mechanism.** demo/color-picker/App.vue:38 — `:action-bar="colorPickerRef?.actionBarContext ?? null"`; colorPickerRef is written only at App.vue:322 inside onDesktopLeftMount. The `?? null` masks "the mobile slot never registered" as "this view has no actions". Breaks VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §7·Picker ("Copy lives once in the action region") and §3 law 6 (mobile is a stage→inspector→ACTION sequence beneath the same top dock).

**Evidence.**

```
D-dock-probe4.mjs, complete button inventory of /#/ at 390x844: hasCopyColor:false hasRandom:false hasReset:false hasOpenColorInput:false actionBarLayerPresent:false; docBtnNames = ["Save edit","Cancel edit","Switch to slug","Generate new slug","Cancel","Select view","Toggle action bar","Picker","About","Menu","Login","@mbabb","Select color space","l channel","a channel","b channel","alpha channel"]. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · R3-02 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** No cancel path exists, and a 2000 ms commit debounce means valid input typed and blurred inside two seconds is silently discarded with zero signal.

**Mechanism.** Two sources of truth (contenteditable text vs. model) reconciled only by a long debounce and an unconditional blur repaint, with no cancel gesture and no uncommitted-state affordance.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:92 `debounce(parseAndSetColor, 2000)`; ColorInput.vue:202-211 handles only `Enter`; :183-193 blur repaints from the model. Measured, frames/r3probe2.json: `"cancel":{"typed":"rebeccapurple","afterEsc":{"text":"rebeccapurple","focused":true},"afterBlur":"lab(92% 88.8 20 / 82.7%)","escapeCancels":false,"blurCommitted":false}`.
```

**Reproduction.** Open the field -> select all -> type `rebeccapurple` (valid CSS) -> press Escape (nothing happens) -> click elsewhere within 2 s. The value reverts to the previous colour with no error, no toast, no 'unsaved' mark.

**Proposed cure.** Escape restores the model value and exits; blur either commits or warns but never silently discards; drop the debounce to a live-preview cadence (~150 ms) once the field is no longer the sole commit path. ### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The component hand-applies GlassDock's PRIVATE shell-pane classes (`.dock-layer` + `is-active`/`is-leaving`) to arbitrary consumer components. In Glass 7 the public face class is `.dock-face`; `.dock-layer` is emitted only by GlassDock's own two internal plates. Because every `.dock-layer` rule is scoped `:where(.glass-dock, .dock-layer-group) .dock-layer`, the counterfeit faces match the dock's private plate rules — including two that are actively hostile during a dock morph.

**Mechanism.** consumer styles itself from producer internals — a silent breakage contract, since no public API ever promised these class names

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/layers/ActionBarLayer.vue:91. Scan of the producer bundle: `python3 -c "...re.finditer(r'dock-layer(?![-a-z])', open('dist/dock.js').read())..."` returns exactly two emission sites, both internal: `class: L(["dock-layer dock-layer--full", {...}])` and `class: L(["dock-layer dock-layer--summary", {...}])`. The public face component emits `class: L(["dock-face", { "is-active": ..., "is-le..." }])`. Hostile rules in layers.css: `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-leaving { opacity: calc(1 - var(--dock-morph-t)); }` and `.glass-dock[data-morphing] .dock-layer.is-active > * { opacity: var(--child-reveal); scale: calc(0.82 + 0.18 * var(--child-reveal)); }`.
```

**Reproduction.** grep the emission sites as above; then on the live page confirm the consumer nodes carry the class: the two `.dock-layer-grid` children report className `"flex items-center justify-around flex-1 dock-layer is-active"` and `"grid grid-cols-1 gap-y-2 p-0 m-0 dock-layer min-w-0"`. (The compound swap-during-dock-morph symptom is a HYPOTHESIS — the rules and the class match are both confirmed, but I did not capture a simultaneous frame.)

**Proposed cure.** Same transposition as D-1 — `<DockLayer>` faces inside `<DockCrossfade>` carry the producer's own `.dock-face` packaging, so the consumer stops naming producer internals at all.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The trigger renders an EMPTY label on 7 of 14 routes and simultaneously wears the admin gold identity on /atmosphere and /blob, which are not admin surfaces; the open menu reports `aria-selected=false` on every option, i.e. "no selection", while the app is on a route.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured webkit 1440x900 (isDesktop true), scratchpad/D-probe3.json: labels `Home|Palettes|Browse|Extract|Mix|Generate|Gradient` for the 7 user routes; label="" and goldIcon=true for /atmosphere, /blob, /admin/users, /admin/names, /admin/audit, /admin/flagged, /admin/tags, while document.title reads e.g. "Atmosphere — Color Picker". Menu open on /#/atmosphere: all 7 options aria-selected="false". Corroborated by the tracked real-Safari shot docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/atmosphere.png. Mechanism: useDockAdminMode.ts:34-40 gates the option set on `isAdminMode && isAdminAuthenticated` while :56-60 flips `isAdminMode` on route alone; DockViewSelect.vue:70,80 consume `isAdminMode` alone. ```

**Reproduction.** open http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere unauthenticated -> dock shows gold sparkle + chevron, no text; open the menu -> 7 options, none selected. Repro script: scratchpad/D-dvs-probe3.mjs

**Proposed cure.** One enumeration, one predicate. Add `audience: "public" | "admin"` to `demo/shell/viewSchema.ts` (which already types every view) and derive BOTH the option set and the mode flag from it, so no state can exist where the value has no option. Promote /atmosphere and /blob to public member routes, as VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:58 already declares them, and delete the route-shaped admin guess.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The failure-explicit Result contract is destroyed at the demo boundary, so a LIBRARY CRASH and a USER TYPO are the same event. src/css/grammar.ts:181 throws TypeError on eight inputs; demo/color-session/picker-color.ts:109-113 is a throwing facade that only handles `result.ok === false` and lets the raw TypeError escape past its own typed PickerColorError; demo/color-session/useColorParsing.ts:80-85 catches everything with a bare `catch {}` and renders the hardcoded literal 'not a valid color'. Re-derived and confirmed this pass; first filed by the prior pass.

**Mechanism.** Contract transposition, three hops, each lossy: Result → exception (picker-color.ts valueOrThrow/PickerColorError) → bare catch {} (useColorParsing) → a constant string literal (ColorInput.vue:88). The discriminant is erased at every hop. Two further silencers compound it: `initialParse` (useColorParsing.ts:83) suppresses a composable's first failure, and `previousInvalid` (useColorParsing.ts:62) makes any REPEAT of the same string a total no-op — the state a frustrated user reaches within two seconds.

**Evidence.**

```
Contract: src/css/types.ts:25-27 (`ParseResult<T> = {ok:true,...} | {ok:false, diagnostics:[ParseIssue,...]}`), package.json:4 ('failure-explicit'). Throw site: src/css/grammar.ts:181 `splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space")` where splitTopLevel("","/") returns [] (grammar.ts:79,85). Measured against the exact dist the dev server serves (dist/subpaths/css.js, Jul 24 14:04, newer than src/css/grammar.ts Jul 17 14:48): all of oklch() rgb() hsl() lab() lch() color() oklab() 'hsl(  )' THROW `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`, while 'oklch(' and 'notacolor' correctly return ok:false. Live at http://localhost:9000/#/ after typing oklch()+Enter: {"inputText":"oklch()","errorBadge":null,"borderColor":"lab(92 88.8 20 / 0.827)"} and browser_console_messages(level=error) → Errors: 0. Diagnostics loss is total: ParseIssue carries {code,start,end,expected,actual} (src/css/types.ts:10-24) and the only three demo readers of `.diagnostics` are internal-invariant sites with no human present (useGradientCSS.ts:128, useImageSampler.ts:60, useMarkdownColors.ts:33); the one surface where a human types CSS reads it never.
```

**Reproduction.** `npx vitest run --config docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/shell-dock-colorinput/probe.vitest.config.ts` → 5/5 green. The harness drives the REAL useColorParsing composable and the REAL picker-color facade against the PUBLISHED dist/subpaths/{color,css}.js and proves: (1) all eight throw while 'oklch(' returns ok:false — the crash is narrower than the failure path and therefore invisible beside it; (2) parsePickerColor re-throws a raw TypeError, not PickerColorError; (3) with the initialParse gate burned, all eight leave the model object-identical (toBe) and set the same boolean a typo sets; (4) the first parse of a composable's life leaves parseError===false; (5) a repeat of the same crasher early-returns on previousInvalid — no badge, no console, no model change. Live: the gesture chain above.

**Proposed cure.** Delete valueOrThrow and PickerColorError from picker-color.ts and every bare catch on the parse path. parseCssColor already returns the right shape — let it reach the component: `parsePickerColor(s): ParseResult<CssColor>`; `useColorParsing.commit(source)` returns it; ColorInput renders `diagnostics[0].expected` and marks [start,end] in the field. No try, no catch, no previousInvalid cache. An unexpected TypeError then has nowhere to hide — it becomes a page error the existing visual-audit harness already reports, so 'pageErrors — 0' becomes a real green instead of a manufactured one.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-30 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** A failed login is completely silent: the slug-edit layer closes as if it succeeded, and there are three independent, redundant reasons no error can reach the user. (1) `SlugEditLayer.vue:54` calls `pm.onSlugSwitch(...)` with no `await` inside a `try`, while `useSlugMigration.ts:51` declares it `async` — the `catch` at :57 is unreachable, and :55-56 close the layer synchronously before the network call resolves. (2) It would not matter: the callee catches everything itself (`useSlugMigration.ts:74-88`) and dispatches onto `slugBarRef.value?.setError(...)`, a permanently-null ref. (3) `slugError` is written at six sites in SlugEditLayer and rendered at zero — the template contains no reference to it. And the substring branches at :59-62 are a verbatim resurrection of the exact bug `useSlugMigration.ts:77-82` records as killed at S.W2 W2-6 (`ApiProblem` does `super(title)`, so `e.message` is the server title and can never contain '409'/'404'/'429').

**Mechanism.** error channel swallowed three ways: un-awaited async across a component boundary; callee catches into a null instance ref; error state with no template binding — plus a condemned string-sniff re-authored after its cure was recorded

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/layers/SlugEditLayer.vue:54 (un-awaited) · :57 (catch) · :59-62 (substring sniff) · :13,18,43,49,59-62 (slugError writes) · `sed -n '74,119p' SlugEditLayer.vue | grep slugError` → no output (never rendered). demo/palettes/useSlugMigration.ts:51 (`async function onSlugSwitch`) · :77-82 (the S.W2 W2-6 ruling comment) · :84-87 (correct typed path, dispatched into null). demo/platform/transport/api-problem.ts:22-33 (`super(title)`). LIVE REPRODUCTION (LDOCK-probe6.mjs, WebKit 1440x900, http://localhost:9000): after filling 'aaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd' and clicking button[aria-label="Switch to slug"] — `[after submit] inputValue:"" layerInert:true layerAriaHidden:"true" errorish:[]`, dock still shows 'Login', console tail contains only the two boot lines, no error from the login attempt.
```

**Reproduction.** node LDOCK-probe6.mjs (scratchpad) against the live dev server at http://localhost:9000 — open the dock Login button, fill the slug input, submit; observe layer closes inert+aria-hidden, input cleared, zero error text anywhere in the DOM (`errorish: []`), clean console. The dev server's API is deliberately misconfigured (its own status lamp reads 'dev misconfigured'), so the attempt is guaranteed to fail.

**Proposed cure.** `onSlugSwitch` returns its outcome (`Promise<Result<void, ApiProblem>>`) instead of dispatching it onto a component instance; the layer awaits and renders the failure. One contract change removes all three swallows at once — awaiting makes it observable, returning kills the instance-ref channel, rendering kills the dead state. Rides L-6/L-24's move of the session port to `demo/platform/auth/`, so the login surface becomes a function with a typed result rather than a feature-owned side effect.

**Defect.** Primary navigation renders a combobox with no selected option on 7 of 14 named routes. The option set and the model value have different owners; membership is never enforced.

**Mechanism.** Duplicated ownership of one concept (the view taxonomy) across two modules, with no relation expressed in the type system, the schema, or the tests. viewSchema.ts owns label/icon/hue/panes/defaultPaneIndex for all 14 views but carries NO nav-grouping field — so the dock had to re-enumerate, and the re-enumeration can disagree.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/shell/dock/DockViewSelect.vue:52 binds :model-value="currentView" (range = 14 ViewIds, from viewSchema.ts:36-50 via useViewManager) while :92-97 renders one SelectItem per viewEntries (range = 7, from useDockAdminMode.ts:26-27). Live Playwright, http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere: {triggerText:"", triggerRole:"combobox", triggerRectW:60}; listbox opened → {optionCount:7, anySelected:false, activeDescendant:null}. Control /#/browse → {triggerText:"Browse", triggerRectW:117}. Screenshots: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/{atmosphere,admin-users}.png show icon+chevron with no label; browse.png shows "Browse". reka-ui SelectValue.js:33-42 returns "" when modelValue is absent from optionsSet; placeholder defaults to "".
```

**Reproduction.** Open http://localhost:9000/#/atmosphere (or /#/blob or any /#/admin/*) unauthenticated at >=1024px width. document.querySelector('.view-select-trigger').textContent === "". Click it; every [role=option] has aria-selected="false" and the trigger's aria-activedescendant is null. Compare /#/browse.

**Proposed cure.** Add `nav: "primary" | "admin"` to PaneConfig in demo/shell/viewSchema.ts — the table that already owns every other per-view fact. useDockAdminMode becomes a filter over VIEW_MAP (entries = viewsInGroup(activeGroup) ∪ {currentView}); the two literal arrays die. currentView ∈ viewEntries then holds BY CONSTRUCTION for every view, because both sides read one table. The invariant becomes a theorem rather than an untested assumption.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2/L-3/L-17 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The "is this view admin?" predicate is implemented seven times across five files with three different populations, and one of the seven (router meta.admin) has zero readers.

**Mechanism.** No owner for the authorisation/grouping concept. Taxonomy encoded in a NAMING CONVENTION (startsWith("admin-")) at four sites — silently wrong the moment a view is renamed — plus a literal array, plus inert route metadata.

**Evidence.**

```
(1) demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:31-35 meta:{admin:true} on 5 routes — `grep -rn "meta.admin|beforeEach|beforeResolve|addRoute" demo/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue'` → NO OUTPUT, zero consumers. (2) useDockAdminMode.ts:27 adminViews = 7 ids (adds atmosphere, blob). (3) useDockAdminMode.ts:32 startsWith("admin-") = 5. (4) useDockAdminMode.ts:56 adminViews.includes = 7. (5) usePaletteWiring.ts:166-171 startsWith("admin-"), watch with NO {immediate:true} unlike the watch at :144-155. (6) usePaneRouter.ts:93,140 startsWith("admin-"). (7) AdminPane.vue:91 a hand-written 5-member union. viewSchema.ts:172,181 gives atmosphere/blob PRIMARY hue shifts 280/320, contradicting its own comment at :69-71 that admin views stay at 0.
```

**Reproduction.** grep -rn "meta.admin|beforeEach|beforeResolve|addRoute" demo/ --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' → no output. Then open /#/admin/users in a fresh profile: the full admin console renders (Users · Manage accounts and permissions, search, Prune empty, Refresh) while the dock still reads "Login" — captured at shots/safari-desktop-light/admin-users.png; REPORT.md:128-132 records main=1 and 244-273 chars for all five admin routes in every matrix, unauthenticated. The eviction watch at usePaletteWiring.ts:167 cannot fire because there is no true→false transition on a cold deep-link.

**Proposed cure.** The same single `nav` field is the sole home. Derive router meta at construction (meta:{admin: VIEW_MAP[name].nav==="admin"}); replace all four startsWith sites and AdminPane's union with reads of VIEW_MAP[v].nav (AdminPane's prop type becomes Extract<ViewId, `admin-${string}`>). Add the ONE reader the dead metadata never had: shell/nav/guard.ts router.beforeEach — which runs per-navigation and therefore covers cold boot by construction, subsuming the non-immediate watch.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The magnifier loupe renders blank on every first show and stays permanently blank on the touch path. `showLoupeAt` flips `loupeVisible` and calls `drawLoupe` in the same synchronous tick, but the canvas is behind `v-if="loupe.loupeVisible.value"`, so `loupeCanvasRef.value` is still null and the draw is silently skipped. Since `onTap` also sets `pinned=true`, `onHover` (the only path that would repaint) returns early forever.

**Mechanism.** synchronous paint into a v-if element that Vue has not flushed to the DOM yet (mount/paint ordering race)

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/extract/ImageEyedropper/composables/useLoupeCanvas.ts:55-60 (showLoupeAt) and :27-30 (drawLoupe early return); ImageEyedropper.vue:78-86 (v-if + canvas). MEASURED (probe2 §A): A_pinned {loupeVisible:true, loupeNonZeroPx:9604, di110:2} → Escape → A_tapNoHover {loupeVisible:true, loupeNonZeroPx:0, di110:2} → A_afterOneMove {loupeNonZeroPx:0, di110:2}. Independent replication (probe4): {"pointermoves":40,"getImageDataCalls":40,"loupeDraws":39} — the missing draw is the first. Visual: .playwright-mcp/eyedropper-live.png shows an empty green-ringed circle.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/extract → upload any image → click the preview to open the eyedropper → tap once WITHOUT moving the pointer first (i.e. any touch tap). The loupe appears and is empty; it never fills. Scripted: .playwright-mcp/probe2.js section A.

**Proposed cure.** Keep the loupe canvas permanently mounted and gate visibility on opacity/visibility instead of v-if. This kills the race by construction, lets the already-declared `.loupe { transition: opacity }` (ImageEyedropper.vue:270 — currently dead CSS) actually run, and removes a DOM create/destroy from the hover path. (`await nextTick()` before drawLoupe is the patch, not the cure.)

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `justUnpinned` is a component-scope latch whose only exit is inside `onTap`; a drag never reaches `onTap`, so after pin → press-drag → release the flag stays true and the NEXT legitimate tap is silently swallowed.

**Mechanism.** cross-handler boolean latch with a single clear site that one of two gesture terminations never reaches

**Evidence.**

```
ImageEyedropper.vue:123 (`let justUnpinned = false`), :151-155 (onTap's only clear), :176-185 (capture-phase pointerdown sets it); useInertiaGesture.ts:277-281 (onTap fires only when !hasMoved). MEASURED (probe-eyedropper.js): tapRed buttons=3 (pinned) → afterDrag buttons=1 → tapTransparent_1st buttons=1 (TAP SWALLOWED) → tapTransparent_2nd buttons=3. Cross-check: Escape-unpin (:226-235) does NOT set the flag and the next tap pins immediately (probe2 A_afterEscape buttons 1 → A_tapNoHover buttons 3).
```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper, tap to pin a color, then press and drag (this unpins and pans), release, then tap somewhere new — the tap does nothing; a second tap is required. Scripted: .playwright-mcp/probe-eyedropper.js.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the flag and fold unpin into useInertiaGesture's own state machine, which already tracks hasMoved/isPanning. 'A pointerdown while pinned suppresses the pointerup that ends THIS gesture' has a definite lifetime inside the gesture; as a component-scope boolean it has none.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Dragging (or shift+arrow nudging) a handle past a neighbour leaves `stops` non-monotonic: the rail's ramp positions descend so CSS clamps them into a flat band, the easing intervals now straddle inverted pairs, and the serialized CSS is refused by the app's own parser — the atomic round-trip contract is one-way only.

**Mechanism.** Sortedness is enforced on insert and merely coincidental on update — the position write is a raw array map, so an invariant the rest of the system depends on has no owner.

**Evidence.**

```
Live: after adding a stop at 50% and dragging the 0% handle right, DOM/model order = ["Gradient stop at 75%","Gradient stop at 50%","Gradient stop at 100%"]; editor text = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 74.9%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`; rail background-image head = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 74.9%, oklch(0.746875 0.150937 148.75) 73.34%, oklch(0.74375 0.151875 152.5) 71.79%, …)` (descending). `npx vite-node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/parse-probe.ts` → `parseGradientCSS -> reject: stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)` on that exact string. Code: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (updateStop never sorts) vs :118 (addStop does); emit sites GradientStopEditor.vue:145 and :179; guard-on-input at demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse.ts:284-290.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000 → dock → Gradient → click the rail at 50% → drag the 0% handle to ~75% → read the CSS box and the rail's computed background-image; paste that CSS back into the editor and the app rejects it.

**Proposed cure.** Make ordering a property of the operation, not of the array: one model action `setStopPosition(id, pos)` that maps then sorts, so sortedness is total by construction, paired with C2's identity-keyed intervals so the re-sort cannot scramble easing. Clamping the drag to (prev, next) is cheaper and strictly worse — it makes stops un-reorderable.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Easing intervals are keyed by array INDEX and synced by a length watcher that appends/truncates at the TAIL, while addStop inserts in sorted position — so inserting a stop silently moves the user's authored curve onto a different pair of stops and reverts the authored segment to linear.

**Mechanism.** An adjacency relation (which pair of stops a curve belongs to) is modelled as a positional array, and the sync watcher observes only `stops.length`, so it cannot know where the stop landed and always guesses 'at the end'.

**Evidence.**

```
Live: stops [0,50,100] with `steps(4, jump-end)` authored on segment 50→100 → readouts ["cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)","steps(4, jump-end)"], heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps"]. After clicking the rail at 25%: labels [0%,25%,50%,100%], readouts ["cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)","steps(4, jump-end)","cubic-bezier(0, 0, 1, 1)"], heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps","3 → 4linear"] — steps now governs 25→50; the authored 50→100 curve is gone. Code: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:89-100.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000 → Gradient → click the rail at 50% → open interval row 2 → click the `steps` specimen → click the rail at 25% → read `.readout-rail code` and `.interval-head` text.

**Proposed cure.** Hang the interval on the stop that OPENS it — `GradientStop { id, cssColor, position, easing }` (last stop's easing ignored) — so the curve travels with its own stop through any insert/remove/sort. That deletes the parallel array, the sync watcher, and all three `Gradient interval N is missing` throws (useGradientCSS.ts:189/240, GradientVisualizer.vue:77). Alternative: a Map keyed by the ordered stop-id pair.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Pressing any `back`-family specimen tile — or dragging a picker control point outside y∈[0,1] — throws and destroys the whole Gradient pane. 3 of 27 catalogue tiles are a live crash in the default app state.

**Mechanism.** missing-domain-boundary: an easing callable's output (a motion value, unbounded) is fed straight into a color-mix progress parameter (a ratio strictly on [0,1]) at three separate sites, with no clamp at the sampling law that owns the domain.

**Evidence.**

```
Probe output: `ease-out-back  rails=[] CRASH=["This panel hit an unexpected error.Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range Try again"]` — same for ease-in-back and ease-in-out-back; linear/ease/steps/step-start/step-end/ease-in-out-expo all CRASH=no. Guard: src/color/operations.ts:88 `if (progress < 0 || progress > 1) return err({ code: "color_progress_out_of_range" });`. Unclamped call sites: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientCSS.ts:199-208 (sampleCoalescedStops), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer/easing/useSpecimenRows.ts:52-59 (fn(0.5)), demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVisualizer.vue:78-85 (colorAtPosition). Measured ranges on the real sampling grid (vite-node against src/subpaths/easing): ease-in-back min=-0.0969 out-of-range 18/33 fn(0.5)=-0.0636; ease-out-back max=1.0868 out-of-range 19/33 fn(0.5)=1.0676; ease-in-out-back min=-0.0923 max=1.0927 out-of-range 21/33. Drag repro: `AFTER DRAG: {"literal":null,"crash":["...color_progress_out_of_range..."]}`. Catalogue built by blind enumeration: easingCatalogue.ts:178 `for (const name of Object.keys(bezierPresets))` with no compatibility filter; GradientEasingEditor.vue:73-76 emits with no validation.
```

**Reproduction.** 1. open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient (easing row `1 → 2` is open on arrival). 2. click the `back` family's `out` tile (`[data-specimen='ease-out-back']`). 3. the entire pane is replaced by the ErrorBoundary reading "This panel hit an unexpected error. Gradient color mix failed: color_progress_out_of_range". Scripted: node scratchpad/wbge-probe4.mjs ease-out-back ease-in-back ease-in-out-back. Recoverable via "Try again" (probe 7: crash 1 → 0, heads back to 1) but all pane state is lost.

**Proposed cure.** Progress into a color mix is a ratio on [0,1] and the sampling law is the ONE place that owns it. Add a private `rampProgress = (t) => Math.min(1, Math.max(0, t))` in useGradientCSS and route sampleCoalescedStops' easedT, useSpecimenRows' fn(0.5) and colorAtPosition's easedT through it — matching CSS's own behaviour (an overshoot timing function on a <color> interpolation clamps to the endpoint colour). The overshoot stays visible where it belongs: in the glyph, which samples the raw callable and needs no clamp, and in the authoring canvas. Do NOT delete the back family — the curves are legitimate and the picker authors them freely; the defect is the missing domain boundary, not the curves.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The component's own stated "zero letterbox" law (O-17 clause 1) is dead code against glass-ui 7.0.0: the picker renders `svg[role="group"]`, not `role="img"`, so `syncVbRatio` no-ops forever and all three `:deep(svg[role="img"])` declarations select nothing. 59.4% of the authoring canvas renders nothing.

**Mechanism.** brittle-producer-dom-coupling: a consumer reaches into a producer's private DOM (an ARIA role attribute) to correct the producer's geometry, and hand-rolls a rAF mirror of state the producer already owns. The glass-ui 7.0.0 adopt changed the role; the coupling failed open and silent.

**Evidence.**

```
EasingAuthoringStage.vue:47-53 queries `svg[role='img']`; :104-115 styles `:deep(svg[role="img"])` with !important. Measured live DOM (probe 5, #easing-authoring-0): `{"svgs":[{"role":"group","aria":"Easing curve 1 → 2","viewBox":"0 -0.1 1 1.2000000000000002","box":{"w":410,"h":200}}],"stageStyleAttr":"--vb-ratio: 1.2;"}` — role is "group". Measured geometry via the oracle's own getScreenCTM method (probe 6): `{"elementBox":{"w":410,"h":200},"drawnPlot":{"w":166.7,"h":200},"letterbox":{"left":121.7,"right":121.7,"top":0,"bottom":0},"vbRatioVar":"1.2","svgComputed":{"aspectRatio":"1 / 1","blockSize":"200px"}}` — computed aspect-ratio is the PRODUCER's inline `1 / 1`, not the seat's `calc(1/1.2)`; block-size is the producer's 200px clamp, not the seat's `auto`. O-17 requires ≤1px on all four edges; measured 121.7px on two. Laws 1 and 2 DO still hold (gridCols "436px", cardShadow "none", cardBackdrop "none") — only the role-keyed law broke, and it broke with no console error, no type error, no exception.
```

**Reproduction.** 1. open http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. 2. press the sliders icon in the readout rail (`aria-label="Author a custom curve"`). 3. inspect `#easing-authoring-0 svg` — role="group", inline style `aspect-ratio: 1 / 1; block-size: clamp(200px, 38cqi, 320px)`. 4. its viewBox is 1×1.2 with preserveAspectRatio=xMidYMid meet in a 410×200 box → drawn plot 166.7×200 centred, 121.7px dead on each side. Scripted: node scratchpad/wbge-probe5.mjs and wbge-probe6.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** Retire the seat override entirely and take the geometry from glass-ui: the picker should expose its live viewBox ratio as a custom property on its own root (a `--easing-vb-ratio` alongside the `--easing-curve-accent` it already stamps, observed in the live DOM) and size its canvas from it. The component header already books this — "the overrides retire at the P7 adopt" — and the adopt has landed (@mkbabb/glass-ui@7.0.0 installed, W44 closed); this is the glass-ui-first edict, the fix belongs upstream. If the producer packet cannot land now, the interim seat must not be able to break in silence: bind to the stable contract (`[data-testid="easing-picker"] svg[viewBox]`) AND make the miss loud — syncVbRatio should console.error on a failed query rather than `return`, so the next producer bump surfaces on first boot instead of in an audit two tranches later.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gen` · C-1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The per-swatch copy verb is entirely dead: `tag="button"`, `:aria-label` and `@click` are all silently discarded by glass-ui 7.0.0's WatercolorDot, which renders a hardcoded aria-hidden span with pointer-events:none. The swatches are not buttons, have no accessible name, are not focusable, and cannot be clicked; copyColor() is unreachable.

**Mechanism.** Producer/consumer contract break absorbed by Vue's legal-fallthrough semantics: a component with inheritAttrs:false that hand-forwards a whitelist of attrs silently swallows every unlisted attr AND every listener, and the type system treats unknown attributes on a component as valid fallthrough. The consumer's documented idiom (tag="button") was never a prop.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gra` · C1 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Drag (and shift+arrow) inverts stop order — the model has no ordering invariant, so the app emits CSS that its own parser rejects and the rail/tile paint a CSS-clamped lie

**Mechanism.** No invariant owner for the ordered-stop model: updateStop is a primitive map() that never re-sorts, while the parser enforces monotonicity on input only. Sortedness is an invariant on insert and a coincidence on drag.

**Evidence.**

```
Live, my own run: afterDrag labels ["Gradient stop at 77%","…50%","…63%","…100%"] (DOM order == model order); rail computed background-image head = linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 76.6%, oklch(0.657192 0.177842 256.369) 74.18%, oklch(0.664384 0.175685 247.739) 71.76%, …) — positions DESCEND. Round-trip: `npx vite-node evidence/parse-probe.ts` → parseGradientCSS -> reject: stop positions must be non-decreasing. Source: demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:127-131 vs the sorting addStop at :118; guard on the way IN at gradientParse.ts:284-290.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/ → set location.hash='#/gradient' in-page → click the rail at 50% → drag the leftmost handle right to ~75%. Read the handle aria-labels in DOM order and getComputedStyle(bar).backgroundImage.

**Proposed cure.** Replace updateStop with one model action that owns ordering totally — setStopPosition(id, position) that maps then .sort((a,b)=>a.position-b.position) — landed together with C2's identity-keyed intervals so the re-sort cannot scramble easing. Sort, do not clamp: clamping to (prev,next) would make a stop un-reorderable.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gra` · C11 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Grab-offset teleport: pressing anywhere but a handle's exact pixel centre and moving the pointer 1 px relocates the stop by the whole grab offset

**Mechanism.** onHandlePointerDown records no grab offset, so the first pointermove snaps the stop centre to the raw pointer. The 4px dead-zone the function already computes (handleGesture.moved) is wired only to the re-tap-to-deselect decision, never to the position emit.

**Evidence.**

```
Live, pasted: RESULT_grab_offset = { grabbed_px_right_of_centre: 8, pointer_travelled_px: 1, handle_travelled_px: 10.12, label_before: "Gradient stop at 0%", label_after: "Gradient stop at 2%" } on a 462px rail. Source: GradientStopEditor.vue:136-146 — emit("update:position", id, getPosition(e)) is absolute and ungated; the hit pseudo that invites the off-centre grab is .rail-handle::before at :374-391 (24px fine / var(--touch-target)=44px coarse).
```

**Reproduction.** Fresh /#/gradient, 2-stop seed. page.mouse.move(handleCentreX + 8, barCentreY); mouse.down(); mouse.move(handleCentreX + 9, barCentreY). Read the handle's aria-label and bounding-box centre before/after.

**Proposed cure.** Capture grabDx = e.clientX - handleCentreX at pointerdown (together with a cached bar rect, which also kills C3's per-move forced layout), gate the first emit on the dead-zone the file already computes (`if (!handleGesture.moved) return;`), and emit positionAt(e.clientX - grabDx). One change retires the teleport, the accidental-nudge class, and half of C3's cost.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gra` · C2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Adding a stop silently re-attaches every authored easing curve to a different pair of stops; removing one does the mirror

**Mechanism.** Intervals are an index-keyed parallel array; the watcher observes only stops.length so it cannot know where the stop landed and always guesses 'at the end'. An adjacency relation modelled as a positional array.

**Evidence.**

```
Live (pass 1, retained): before insert heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps"]; after clicking the rail at 25% heads ["1 → 2linear","2 → 3steps","3 → 4linear"] — steps(4, jump-end) moved from 50%→100% onto 25%→50%. Source: useGradientModel.ts:89-100 (length watcher pushes/truncates at the TAIL) vs addStop at :118 (inserts in SORTED position).
```

**Reproduction.** /#/gradient with stops [0,50,100]; open easing interval row 2, pick the steps specimen; click the rail at 25%; read the interval readouts and row heads.

**Proposed cure.** Hang the interval on the stop that OPENS it — GradientStop { id, cssColor, position, easing }, last stop's easing ignored — so the curve travels with its own stop through any insert/remove/sort. That deletes the intervals array, its sync watcher, and the three 'Gradient interval N is missing' throws (useGradientCSS.ts:189/240, GradientVisualizer.vue:77) outright.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-1 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The sampled color is not the color displayed under the cursor — stage, loupe and sampler use three different resampling rules over the same bitmap, and the displayed color additionally changes with devicePixelRatio while the sample does not.

**Mechanism.** useImageSampler.ts:111-119 sampleAt takes one nearest source texel via Math.floor((rx-panX)/zoom); the visible canvas (ImageEyedropper.vue:69-75) has no image-rendering declaration so the compositor smooths; useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 sets imageSmoothingEnabled=false. No single sampling model.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured composited pixels from probe/shot-desktop-light-pinned.png: (300,560)=[127,0,128], (350,500)=[159,0,96], (301,561)=[183,0,72]. Readout at that location: lab(29.568301979097% 68.287364602547 -112.029709525105) = #0000FF. Measured stage zoom 0.4233. probe/shot-forced-colors.png shows crisp red/blue texels in the loupe and flat purple in the surrounding stage in ONE frame. DPR dependence: same region reads flat purple in shot-desktop-light-pinned.png (DPR 1) and resolved red/blue moire in shot-zoom200.png (DPR 2).
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe/probe.mjs (displayedVsSampled.zoom 0.4233, displayedCentrePixel [95,0,160]) then probe2.mjs (hoverReadout = pure-blue lab). Or by eye: probe/shot-forced-colors.png.

**Proposed cure.** One resampling law owned in one place. zoom>=1: stage paints image-rendering:pixelated so a texel is a visible square and the loupe is that same law magnified. zoom<1: the sample is the area-average over the 1/zoom x 1/zoom source box the pointer's display pixel actually covers. Stage, loupe, reticle and readout then read one SamplerModel instead of three.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Every second tap is a dead tap that also discards the pin, leaving the PREVIOUS color displayed as if it were the current sample. On touch this is the only sampling interaction.

**Mechanism.** ImageEyedropper.vue:176-185 adds a capture-phase pointerdown listener that unpins and raises `justUnpinned`; onTap (:151-155) consumes the flag with an early return. Touch has no hover, so half of all taps are no-ops while the readout keeps showing a color from a different part of the image.

**Evidence.**

```
probe2.mjs tapCycle: tap purple -> lab(29.5683...) pinned(3 buttons); tap grey -> readout UNCHANGED lab(29.5683...), unpinned(1 button); tap grey again -> lab(53.585013452169% 0 0) pinned; tap purple -> readout UNCHANGED lab(53.5850...), unpinned.
```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe2.mjs — see tapCycle table.

**Proposed cure.** Delete justUnpinned and the second, never-removed event-binding mechanism (the composable already binds the element at useInertiaGesture.ts:327-350). A tap always samples and always pins; re-sampling the same texel is idempotent; unpin belongs to Escape/close, which already own it (:226-235).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-5 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** In RTL the specimen canvas is rendered 692px outside its own clipping stage and disappears entirely, while the sampler keeps returning values for an image nobody can see.

```

**Reproduction.** node .../probe/probe4.mjs.

**Proposed cure.** State the specimen's origin instead of inheriting it from flow: absolutely position the canvas at the stage's physical top-left — exactly the frame viewportToImage already assumes. Add dir=ltr / unicode-bidi:isolate on the readout per VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design of demo/workbenches/gradient/GradientVi` · D-2 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** No ordering invariant: a drag can carry a stop across its neighbour, leaving stops[] non-monotonic. sampleCoalescedStops then emits DESCENDING percentages into a CSS linear-gradient, which the browser clamps into a hard band, and the per-interval easing curves silently re-pair because intervals are keyed by array index rather than by the stop pair.

**Evidence.**

```
evidence/p4.mjs T10: `T10 stops after cross {"n":4,"pos":["0","29","8","100"],"centers":[235,362.6,270.6,675]}`; painted rail percentages `[…,26.36, 29, 27.1, 25.2, 23.3, 21.4, 19.5, 17.6, 15.7, 13.8,…]` with `descendingPairs=[[12,29,27.1],…,[21,11.9,10]]`. Screenshot evidence/D02-cross-drag-hard-band.png shows the resulting seam. Source: useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (updateStop never sorts; addStop at :118 does), useGradientCSS.ts:195-200 (pos = s0.position + t*(s1-s0), negative range), GradientVisualizer.vue:64-88 (colorAtPosition assumes sorted). Interval labels stay index-keyed: p2.log T3 `["1 → 2","2 → 3"]`.
```

**Reproduction.** node docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence/p4.mjs — block T10

**Proposed cure.** The model owns the ordinal: re-sort on every position commit and re-key intervals to the stop PAIR, or clamp a dragged stop into (prev, next). Only then is VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §5.2's explicit reorder grammar (Space grabs, 'position of total' announcement, Escape cancels) implementable at all.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The stop-ordering invariant ("positions are non-decreasing") has three owners with three contradictory policies: gradientParse REJECTS violations, addStop SORTS, and updateStop — the mutator this component drives on every pointermove and arrow key — does NOTHING. The result is a live model whose own serializer emits CSS that its own parser rejects, and a rail ramp with decreasing sub-stop positions that CSS clamps into a flat band.

**Mechanism.** unique-semantic-ownership violated — a model invariant enforced by whichever mutator remembers it rather than by the type that carries it

**Evidence.**

```
Owners: gradientParse.ts:284-290 (reject) vs useGradientModel.ts:118 (sort) vs useGradientModel.ts:127-131 (no policy); driven by GradientStopEditor.vue:94,145,179 -> GradientVisualizer.vue:94-96. LIVE (localhost:9000/#/gradient, fresh mount, add stop at 50% then drag first handle to 80%): handles = ["Gradient stop at 80%","Gradient stop at 50%","Gradient stop at 100%"]; CSS readout = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 80%, oklch(70% 0.165 205deg) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)`; computed --rail-ramp = `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(75% …) 80.00%, oklch(74.68% …) 78.13%, oklch(74.37% …) 76.25%, …` (DECREASING). Screenshot: docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-gradient-stopeditor/evidence-rail-after-reorder.png shows the rail as one flat green slab to ~78% with a hard band to blue. LIVE round trip: feeding that CSS back into [aria-label="Gradient CSS"] yields verdict "stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)". HEADLESS: `npx vite-node` on the demo modules -> serialized `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 70%, oklch(0.7 0.16 200) 50%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 100%)` -> re-parse REJECT with the same reason. Untested by the gates: e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:161-172 drags only the MIDDLE handle to 75%, strictly between its neighbours.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient -> click the rail at ~50% (adds a stop) -> drag the leftmost handle to ~80% -> read the CSS box: positions descend (80%, 50%, 100%). Retype that same string into the CSS box -> the destructive verdict appears. Headless equivalent: vite-node script calling updateStop-shaped mutation then serializeGradient -> parseGradientCSS.

**Proposed cure.** Brand the list. A model/stops.ts owns the ordering algebra and is the ONLY producer of an `OrderedStops` (readonly branded array): insertStop / moveStop (re-sorts, stable — the CSS-native behaviour a user expects from dragging past a neighbour) / removeStop. serializeGradient, sampleCoalescedStops and parseGradientCSS all take OrderedStops, so the parser's reject-branch becomes unreachable-by-construction instead of a runtime tripwire aimed at the app itself.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The published `@mkbabb/value.js/css` surface is NOT total: parseCssColor throws a TypeError on eight empty-argument colour functions instead of returning {ok:false}. The demo's entire "library-oracle" architecture (gradientParse.ts header lines 16-17: "validated by the LIBRARY's own parsers — the validity oracles; the demo never hand-validates a color") is therefore structurally unsound, and the throw escapes the model-or-reject contract as an uncaught TypeError.

**Mechanism.** a published API whose type says ParseResult<CssColor> and whose runtime says "or I throw" — partiality hidden behind a non-null assertion; every consumer written against the type is structurally wrong

**Evidence.**

```
Root cause src/css/grammar.ts:181 `const components = splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g," "), "space");` — the non-null assertion over splitTopLevel("","/") which returns []. Consumer gradientParse.ts:92-94 `return parseCssColor(token).ok`. node on working-tree dist/subpaths/css.js: oklch()/rgb()/hsl()/lab()/lch()/oklab()/hwb()/color() all -> `THROW: TypeError Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')`; rgb(1 2 3)/red/oklch(0.7 0.1 30) -> ok. node on the INSTALLED node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 -> same THROW (the bug is in the published package). In-browser dynamic import of the exact aliased module the demo runs -> {"oklch()":"THROW: …","rgb()":"THROW: …","oklch(0.7 0.1 30)":"ok"}. Through the demo parser (npx vite-node): `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT TypeError; `linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT; `linear-gradient(90deg, color(), blue)` -> UNCAUGHT; `linear-gradient(90deg, red, blue)` -> ok.
```

**Reproduction.** npx vite-node with `import { parseGradientCSS } from 'demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/gradientParse'; parseGradientCSS('linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), blue)')` -> uncaught TypeError. Or type that string into the gradient CSS box on a mounted pane.

**Proposed cure.** Totality is the library's contract, not the consumer's try/catch. Replace the non-null assertions in parseFunctionalColor with an explicit empty-body reject (failure(source,"css_syntax",["components"])), and add a property test over {rgb,rgba,hsl,hsla,hwb,lab,lch,oklab,oklch,color} × {""," ","/",",,"} so the surface can never regress to partiality. Do NOT wrap isColorToken in try/catch — that moves the library's contract into its consumer.

**Defect.** `<Button variant="…">` is inert against glass-ui 7 — the component's declared visual hierarchy never renders. glass-ui 7.0.0's ButtonProps has NO `variant` prop; its axis is `emphasis` (primary|secondary|quiet|text) plus `tone`. **Mechanism.** A design-system prop contract enforced by neither the type system nor the runtime. The producer may rename any prop and every consumer keeps compiling and keeps rendering something — worse than breaking, because it is invisible. Aggravated by glass-ui 7's own internal inconsistency: Slider and Badge kept `variant`, only Button moved to `emphasis`.

Call sites: GenerateControls.vue:158 variant="primary-audacious", :166 variant="ghost", :176 variant="ghost". Census: `grep -rn '<Button' -A4 demo/ | grep 'variant=' | wc -l` → 51 (16 ghost, 15 outline, 2 primary-audacious); `grep -rln 'emphasis=' demo/ | wc -l` → 2. `npx vue-tsc -p tsconfig.demo.json --noEmit` → exit 0, no output (green with all 51 sites present).
```

**Reproduction.** Read docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/shots/safari-desktop-light/generate.png: "Regenerate" and the two icon buttons beside it render at IDENTICAL pale weight — three default-emphasis buttons, not one saturated primary flanked by two ghosts. Confirm the cause with the four greps above against glass-ui 7.0.0 in node_modules.

**Proposed cure.** Producer-first, and it belongs in the Glass 8 release gate (G-3), not a 51-site consumer sweep that rots on the next rename: glass-ui closes ButtonProps to unknown attributes, or asserts in dev when a `variant` attr reaches a Button root. Acceptance: `<Button variant="ghost">` FAILS at typecheck or first render, reproducibly in CI. Secondarily reconcile the axis naming across Button/Slider/Badge, since the inconsistency is what made 51 sites wrong by default. Only then sweep the consumers (variant="primary-audacious" → emphasis="primary", variant="ghost" → emphasis="quiet"), leaving Slider/Badge `variant` untouched.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The save seam silently discards the palette name the user types. GenerateControls emits `save: [colors, name]` and passes paletteName, but its sole consumer GeneratePane declares a one-parameter handler and hardcodes the literal "Generated Palette". The editable plate title has no effect on the saved palette.

**Mechanism.** The concept "the name of the thing being saved" has two homes — a ref inside the child and a string literal inside the parent — joined by a Vue emit whose payload the parent is free to ignore silently.

**Evidence.**

```
GenerateControls.vue:48-50 `defineEmits<{ save: [colors: string[], name: string] }>()`; :102-104 `emit("save", [...palette.value], paletteName.value)`. GeneratePane.vue:14-20 `function onSave(colors: string[])` — `name` never bound — then `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)`. TypeScript permits a narrower handler arity, so nothing fails at build. The in-file comment at GenerateControls.vue:44-47 asserts the wire exists ("this emit is already truthful") — the emit is truthful; the wire was never landed.
```

**Reproduction.** Prior seat's live run against http://localhost:9000/#/generate: typed PROBE-NAME-XYZ into the plate title, clicked Save, read localStorage → {"hasProbeName": false, "hasHardcoded": true, sample name:"Generated Palette", slug:"generated-palette-5fd9d37c"}. Static confirmation needs no browser: GeneratePane.vue:14 never destructures the second emit parameter. My own independent re-probe was abandoned — the shared Playwright MCP browser was concurrently driven by parallel seats (my tab was navigated to #/mix mid-evaluation), and I discarded the run rather than report contaminated telemetry.

**Proposed cure.** CURABLE NOW (lands in GeneratePane.vue, outside the pin): bind the second parameter. The idiomatic cure is the L-6 transposition — the name belongs in a provided generate-session where there is no seam to drop it across, making the defect unrepresentable.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 (pass-1, CONFIRMED LIVE by pass 2) · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The palette name the user types is silently discarded on save: the child emits `save: [colors, name]` but the pane's handler declares arity 1 and passes the literal "Generated Palette" to the persistence port. Data loss on user input.

**Mechanism.** Ownership split with an untyped joint: the NAME is owned by the leaf component, the PERSISTENCE PORT (LIBRARY_PORT_KEY) is injected by the parent, and the two are joined by a Vue emit. TypeScript cannot catch it — a handler is always assignable to an emit with more parameters. Second symptom of the same split: `string[] → PaletteColor[]` is synthesised twice (GenerateControls.vue:55-57 and GeneratePane.vue:15-18) because neither file owns 'the generated palette as a domain object'.

**Evidence.**

```
GenerateControls.vue:48-50 `defineEmits<{ save: [colors: string[], name: string] }>()`, :52 `paletteName = ref("Generated Palette")`, :102-104 `emit("save", [...palette.value], paletteName.value)`. GeneratePane.vue:14 `function onSave(colors: string[])` — name parameter never bound — and :19 `pm.createPalette("Generated Palette", paletteColors)`. LIVE REPRODUCTION (pass 2, which pass 1 had to abandon under shared-browser contention): {"url":"http://localhost:9000/#/generate","inputAfterSet":"ZZ-PROBE-NAME","nameMatches":[["color-palettes",["Generated Palette","Sunset","Empty Plate","Overflowing"]]]} — the v-model round-trip is verified and the persisted store contains zero occurrences of ZZ-PROBE-NAME. Comment at :44-47 asserts 'this emit is already truthful' — it is not.
```

**Reproduction.** Playwright at /#/generate with the self-healing hash idiom: set input[aria-label="Palette name"] to ZZ-PROBE-NAME via the native value setter + input event (verified round-trip), click button[aria-label="Save palette"], read localStorage['color-palettes'] → names are ["Generated Palette","Sunset","Empty Plate","Overflowing"].

**Proposed cure.** ESCALATION RECOMMENDED — this is the highest-value action available before Glass 8. GeneratePane.vue is NOT in the hold's pinned receiver set (the four pinned files are ComponentSliders.vue, ConfigSliderPane.vue, ExtractControls.vue, GenerateControls.vue), so binding the second emit argument at GeneratePane.vue:14-19 cures the data loss WITHOUT touching any pinned file. The full cure is the session hoist: `useGenerateSession()` owning preset/harmony/count/seed/name/palette/regenerate/save, provided at the pane under a typed InjectionKey — one writer, one adapter, and the name-drop becomes unrepresentable.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The published library declares its own demo's design system as a runtime dependency, forming a declared package cycle and forcing 5.8 MB of unused install weight on every consumer.

**Mechanism.** wrong-direction dependency declared at the package manifest level: demo-only tooling placed in `dependencies` instead of `devDependencies`, creating value.js → glass-ui → value.js.

**Evidence.**

```
package.json:82-85 `"dependencies": {"@mkbabb/glass-ui":"^7.0.0","@mkbabb/keyframes.js":"^6.0.0"}` — the ONLY two entries. Measured: `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui|@mkbabb/keyframes" src/ | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rn "@mkbabb/glass-ui" dist/subpaths/*.js dist/value.js | wc -l` → 0; `grep -rn "@mkbabb/keyframes" demo/ | wc -l` → 0 (referenced by NOTHING in the repo). `du -sh node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui node_modules/@mkbabb/keyframes.js` → 5.2M + 608K, against dist/subpaths at 132K. glass-ui/package.json peerDependencies includes `"@mkbabb/value.js":"^4.0.0"`.
```

**Reproduction.** `npm i @mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0` in an empty non-Vue project: the install pulls a Vue design system plus a keyframes engine and glass-ui's own peer set (vue, reka-ui, embla-carousel, tailwindcss, @mkbabb/pencil-boil). `import { CubicBezier } from "@mkbabb/value.js/easing"` uses none of them.

**Proposed cure.** Move both entries to `devDependencies`. `dependencies` becomes `{}` — the honest shape for a zero-runtime-dependency value library. Nothing breaks: `"files": ["dist", "!dist/gh-pages", …]` (package.json:49-53) never ships the demo.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The gradient domain model — including a headless CSS parser with zero Vue in it — is typed by a Vue component's v-model payload imported from the design system.

**Mechanism.** inverted semantic ownership: the concept 'an authored easing curve = mode + re-parseable CSS literal + resolved callable + raw params' is a value.js concept, but value.js publishes no such record, so its own demo borrows one from a package that depends on it.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/workbenches/gradient/composables/useGradientModel.ts:49 `export type GradientInterval = EasingPickerValue;` (imported from `@mkbabb/glass-ui/easing` at line 12). glass-ui's own declaration calls it "The picker's v-model payload" (node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/components/easing/composables/useEasingPicker.d.ts). It propagates into UI-free code: gradientParse.ts:41 `interface ParsedGradientModel { …; intervals: GradientInterval[] }` (that module has zero Vue imports); useGradientCSS.ts:53-62,120-133,232-254; and the subject's own public contract GradientEasingEditor.vue:48-50 `"update-interval": [index: number, value: EasingPickerValue]`.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE (latent). Failure scenario: glass-ui 8 renames `term`→`jump` or makes `points` optional for steps mode — a semver-legal design-system component change. That silently breaks value.js's headless gradient CSS parser, its serializers and its persisted model shape, none of which involve a picker.

**Proposed cure.** value.js `/easing` mints the record: `export interface AuthoredEasing { readonly mode: "bezier"|"steps"; readonly css: string; readonly fn: EasingFunction; readonly points: readonly [number,number,number,number]; readonly steps: number; readonly term: JumpPosition }`. Then `GradientInterval = AuthoredEasing` (no glass-ui import in the model at all) and glass-ui narrows to `export type EasingPickerValue = AuthoredEasing` — consuming the library's vocabulary, the direction its peerDeps already declare. The glass-ui type imports at useGradientModel.ts:12, easingCatalogue.ts:31-35 and GradientEasingEditor.vue:30 all collapse to `@mkbabb/value.js/easing`.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The stop-ordering invariant is homeless: three write paths into stops[] with three contradictory policies. addStop sorts (useGradientModel.ts:118); parseGradientCSS rejects violations (gradientParse.ts:284-290); updateStop — the path this component drives from drag (:94,:145) and keyboard (:179) — enforces nothing (useGradientModel.ts:127-131). The model's serializer therefore emits CSS its own parser calls unmodelable, and intervals[i], defined as the span between stops[i] and stops[i+1], ends up attached to an inverted span.

**Mechanism.** Unique semantic ownership violated — position semantics live in the leaf component (pixels/keys → number), array identity lives in the model, the ordering law lives in the parser. One concept, three homes; the invariant died in the seam. Root structural cause is L-3: hand-rolling a multi-thumb slider instead of consuming one.

**Evidence.**

```
Live at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient, fresh mount, keyboard only — 10x shift+ArrowRight on stops[0] then 10x shift+ArrowLeft on stops[1] yields labels ["Gradient stop at 100%","Gradient stop at 0%"] and CSS readout `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 100%, oklch(0.65 0.18 265) 0%)` with errs: []. Feeding that exact string to the app's own parser in-page: `import('/@fs/…/gradientParse.ts').parseGradientCSS(...)` → "REJECT: stop positions must be non-decreasing (hard-stop reordering isn't modeled)"; the ordered control case returns OK. Computed --rail-ramp came out with DECREASING positions (100.00%, 96.88%, …, 3.13%, 0.00%), which CSS Images 3 §3.4.3 colour-stop fixup silently repairs. Coverage: `grep -rn "non-decreasing|monotonic" e2e test` finds the invariant only in the parser and its unit test; e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:144 drags but never asserts order.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/gradient → focus the 0% stop handle → shift+ArrowRight x10 → focus the other handle → shift+ArrowLeft x10 → read the CSS box. Positions descend. Retype that string into the CSS box and the destructive parse verdict appears.

**Proposed cure.** Do NOT add .sort() to updateStop — that makes a fourth policy holder. Transpose the instrument: bind stop positions to a multi-thumb glass-ui Slider (variant="stops"), where the invariant is already solved, shipped and installed one import line away — node_modules/reka-ui/dist/Slider/SliderRoot.js:124 calls getNextSortedValues on every commit, utils.js:8 sorts. Ordering becomes structurally unrepresentable rather than guarded.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-2 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** parseGradientCSS is documented total ("model-or-reject … never a partial", gradientParse.ts:5-6) and is not: it delegates validity to a non-total library oracle. gradientParse.ts:16-17 explicitly names parseCssColor/parseCssScalar "the validity oracles; the demo never hand-validates a color". parseCssColor throws instead of returning {ok:false} for 8 empty-argument colour functions, so isColorToken (gradientParse.ts:92-94) is a crash site and the throw escapes the whole model-or-reject contract. The /css subpath publishes a ParseResult-typed API — a type-level promise of totality — and breaks it.

**Mechanism.** A published boundary whose type says ParseResult<CssColor> and whose runtime says "or I throw". The consumer built its own totality guarantee on a guarantee never given, and no structural check exists that would catch the gap.

**Evidence.**

```
In-page, against the real module: `parseGradientCSS('linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), red)')` → THROW: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace'); same for rgb() and color-mix(). Library site confirmed by `grep -n "replace(/,/g" src/css/grammar.ts` → line 181: `const components = splitTopLevel(slash[0]!.replace(/,/g, " "), "space");` — a `!` non-null assertion over splitTopLevel("", "/") which returns [].
```

**Reproduction.** Type `linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(), red)` into the gradient CSS editor at http://localhost:9000/#/gradient. Chain: GradientCodeEditor.onInput → debouncedParse (GradientCodeEditor.vue:55) → emit("parse") → GradientVisualizer.onParseCSS (:102) → applyCSS → parseGradientCSS. The parseVerdict UI that e2e/smoke/views/gradient.spec.ts:222 certifies ("garbage input fails LOUD") never runs — these 8 inputs fail silently and wrongly.

**Proposed cure.** Totality is the library's contract and belongs in the library: parseFunctionalColor must return failure(source) on an empty body, plus a property test over {fn} × {"", " ", "/", ",,"} so the surface cannot regress to partiality. Explicitly do NOT wrap isColorToken in a try/catch — that is a masking fallback (edict 2) and moves the library's contract into its consumer.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / owners` · L-1 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The loupe canvas has two owners: `useLoupeCanvas` holds its ref by template-string (`useTemplateRef("loupeCanvasRef")`) while `ImageEyedropper.vue` owns the element's existence with `v-if`. `showLoupeAt` flips the flag and calls `drawLoupe` synchronously, so the ref is still null and the draw silently early-returns. On touch there is no follow-up pointermove and `hideLoupe` unmounts the element again, so the magnifier NEVER paints.

**Mechanism.** ownership split — element lifetime owned by the template, element reference owned by a composable, joined only by a string name and by Vue's flush ordering

**Evidence.**

```
useLoupeCanvas.ts:21 (useTemplateRef by string), :30 (silent early return), :56-59 (flip + synchronous draw); ImageEyedropper.vue:78,85 (v-if owns the element). jsdom+Vue reproduction output: 'sample #1 … drawLoupe() sees loupeCanvasRef = null -> EARLY RETURN, no paint' / 'after nextTick: <canvas>' / 'sample #2 … -> paints'. Visual: probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png shows the loupe ring fully transparent — the fixture's purple/grey edge continues through the circle at 1:1 scale, not the 10x blow-up a painted loupe would show.
```

**Reproduction.** node --input-type=module -e '<appendix A2 in the report>' — prints the null-ref early return on sample #1. Independently visible in docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/components/wb-extract-imageeyedropper/probe/shot-mobile-dark-tapped.png.

**Proposed cure.** Do not split existence from reference. The DPR-correct, paint-on-demand 2D surface is a design-system primitive: glass-ui `./canvas` publishes `useCanvas2D`/`useCanvasLifecycle` (loop-shaped) and needs a paint-on-demand sibling; the loupe becomes a `Loupe.vue` that owns its canvas outright through it. Relay the glass-ui half to the BH inbox per the standing relay invariant.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-picke` · C-2 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The mobile pane slot is the only slot with no `:on-mount`, so colorPickerRef / generatePaneRef / gradientPaneRef / mixPaneRef are permanently null at mobile viewports. Nine dock action-bar actions render, accept clicks, and silently do nothing; the picker's action bar and the dock commit/cancel-edit affordances are dead on mobile.

**Mechanism.** Ref capture is wired per-slot by hand and one slot was missed; every consumer then optional-chains (`?.`) into the nulls, so the structural gap degrades silently instead of failing. usePaletteWiring.ts:65-73/:121-127 add masking fallbacks (edict 2) that hide it further.

```
Same script, same selectors, two viewports: desktop-1440 /#/generate — dock button[aria-label='Regenerate'] scoped to nav.dock-band → palette seed 05a86311 → e84f5064 (works); mobile-390 /#/generate → seed f16915bd → f16915bd (dead), while the pane's own Regenerate on the same page changes it f16915bd → e04dde63 (control passes). At 390px on /#/ the picker's `.action-bar-toggle-inner` measures zero width (toggleVisible=false) vs true at 1440px. Code: App.vue:83-91 (mobile slot, no :on-mount) vs App.vue:105/:131; refs assigned only in App.vue:323-332; handlers optional-chain into null at usePaneRouter.ts:196-198/:208-210/:220-222; App.vue:38 and :41-42 read the null ref; usePaletteWiring.ts:37-58/:117 turns its 2s race-guard into the guaranteed path.

PaneSlot already owns `liveKey`: have it call `onMount(instance, liveKey)` and let App store into one `paneRefs` record keyed by pane name — one path for mobile and both desktop slots, with the slot (not a second source of truth) answering 'which ref'. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-picke` · C-3 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The ref-capture callback fills the WRONG ref for one frame during a pane swap (a ColorPicker instance lands in generatePaneRef while colorPickerRef is nulled), and it re-fires on every unrelated parent re-render.

Code: App.vue:323-332 reads currentConfig.value.left (the incoming view) while PaneSlot.vue:86-97 delays the rendered triplet by one rAF; PaneSlot.vue:124 builds a fresh arrow `:ref` on every render; App.vue:317-319 declare `ref<any>` so no type error is possible.

```
demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:21-38 = 14 bare string literals. demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:35-49 (`ViewId`) + :104-233 (`VIEW_MAP`) = the same 14. viewSchema.ts:7-11 claims the `router/index.ts` copy was retired at D.W3 Lane D; `grep -n "viewSchema\|ViewId" demo/color-picker/router/index.ts` → (no output) — it was not. Dead third encoding: router/index.ts:31-35 carries `meta:{admin:true}`; `grep -rn "meta\.admin\|meta\?\.admin" demo/` → (no output). The live admin predicate is the string prefix at usePaletteWiring.ts:168, usePaneRouter.ts:93 and :140.
```

**Proposed cure.** Derive routes from VIEW_MAP: `...(Object.keys(VIEW_MAP) as ViewId[]).map(id => ({ path: …, name: id, component: Stub }))` plus the catch-all. Delete `meta.admin`. Replace the `?? "picker"` coercion with a router-level redirect (the catch-all already exists) so an unknown name is a navigation event, not a silent substitution.

Four observations of the same route/viewport class: REPORT.md:119 tracked safari-desktop-light /#/ → canvas=1 (blob ABSENT), consoleErr=1 = "WebGL: context lost." The losing frame is shots/safari-desktop-light/picker.png: no blob, ~230 CSS px empty between the `Lab` identity and the `92.0%, 88.8, 20.0` headline. Asymmetry: the aurora canvas HAS a loss contract — demo/color-picker/composables/boot/useAtmosphere.ts:288,298,301 (`webglcontextlost` / `webglcontextrestored`) — and those are the ONLY matches in the tree (`grep -rn 'webglcontextlost|contextlost|isContextLost|contextrestored' demo/ src/`). The blob has none. App.vue:296 owns the DAG; useOverture.ts:28-40 gates B4 on "B3-complete AND B2-STARTED AND chunk-resolved" with no failed/unavailable arm. Canon: PROPORTION-AUDIT.md:59 (PR-15) and VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:182 "The headline->next-instrument interval is not dead acreage"; :142 "The CSS ground is the honest first frame. Aurora/Blob enhance it after paint without geometry change."

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-app-D.mjs (desktop-1440 row → canvases length 1, blob absent) vs node <scratchpad>/probe-overture.mjs (desktop-1440-light → marks include overture:b4@2306ms, canvases include goo-blob-canvas). Re-run either a few times; the outcome flips. Static: REPORT.md:17,119,134 and shots/safari-desktop-{light,dark}/picker.png side by side.

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/color-picker/App.vue, the app sh` · D-8 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** The document never scrolls at any viewport — the shell is a fixed overflow:hidden viewport frame — so every route's overflow is forced into nested card scroll wells, up to 7251px deep behind a backdrop-filter. The canon requires mobile to be one document-scrolling sequence.

**Mechanism.** a viewport-locked shell (100dvh + overflow:hidden) that displaces the document scroller into per-card wells, inverting the canon's scroll ownership

**Evidence.**

```
VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:32 (§3 law 6): "Mobile uses one document-scrolling stage->inspector->action sequence beneath the same top dock." Measured on all three matrices (probe-app-D.mjs): desktop-1440 docScrollable 0 / bodyScrollable 0 / appLayoutOverflow "hidden/hidden h=900px"; zoom200-720x450 0 / 0 / "hidden/hidden h=450px"; mobile-390x844 0 / 0 / "hidden/hidden h=843.98px". Source: demo/styles/shell.css:19-28 `.app-layout { height: 100dvh; overflow: hidden; }` plus shell.css:75 `max-height: var(--content-max-h)` resolving to clamp(30rem,62dvh,38rem) on the mobile arm (foundation.css:481). Consequence measured at desktop /#/: `scrollables = ["div.glass-resting.card +7251px"]` — 7251px of content inside a 774px card, behind the shell.css:196-208 backdrop-filter carrier, with the page scrollbar suppressed.
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-app-D.mjs  → all three rows report docScrollable 0 and bodyScrollable 0; the desktop-1440 row reports scrollables ['div.glass-resting.card +7251px'].

**Proposed cure.** The shell's block axis becomes `min-height: 100dvh` and the document scrolls. The dock band keeps its reserved band via `position: sticky` on grid row 1 — §3 law 4 is already satisfied structurally by `--dock-band-min-h` (shell.css:44) — so the reservation survives without the `overflow: hidden` that costs the document its scroll.

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/color-picker/App.vue, the app sh` · D-9 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** App.vue's boot contract is split across a file it does not own and duplicated in two languages. It mounts onto `<body>` as a three-root fragment, depends on three host attributes declared in index.html (one of which is provably dead), makes the canon's required static boot-error region structurally impossible to preserve, and re-runs the prepaint script's URL/storage/default precedence a second time in TypeScript — which §6.2 forbids in those words.

**Mechanism.** split root ownership — the component's own root contract (positioning ancestor, material attribute, boot precedence) lives in the entry HTML, so it is untyped, untestable, invisible to the component, and duplicated

**Evidence.**

```
Measured (probe-app-D.mjs, all three matrices): mountHostIsBody=true, appLayoutParent="body", bodyAttrs=`class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field="" data-v-app=""`, groundState=null. The mount is demo/color-picker/index.html:205-213 (MT-F012's P0 inline module) ending `app.mount("#app")`, and `#app` IS `<body>` (index.html:226). App.vue is a 3-root fragment: div.app-layout (:2), comment nodes (:144-149), MigratePalettesDialog (:152). (1) `class="relative"` is DEAD: the atmosphere canvas (App.vue:9-17, `absolute inset-0`) is a descendant of `.app-layout` (App.vue:2) which is already `position: relative` (shell.css:25), so the nearest positioned ancestor is never `<body>` — a legacy positioning ancestor, owner edict 2. (2) `data-paper-field` is glass-ui's field contract governing App.vue's own descendants incl. portalled dialogs (index.html:222-226) yet is declared where App.vue cannot see it. (3) Mount replaces the host's children, so `<body>` can hold no `<noscript>` and no pre-rendered fallback — while VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:168 requires "A static semantic boot-error region already present in HTML becomes visible through that data state"; measured groundState=null confirms the whole §6.2 latch (data-ground-state / -schema / -store) is unimplemented. (4) index.html:180-200 runs URL/storage/default precedence in vanilla JS writing --saved-bg-0..N; App.vue:231 `resolveHydratedBootModel()` runs URL->storage->default AGAIN in TypeScript (boot/hydrate.ts:53-78) — VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:172: "The hydrated model consumes the frozen boot object ...; it does not repeat scheme/URL/storage precedence, reconstruct an initial palette in TypeScript, or repaint a second 'equivalent' ground."
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-app-D.mjs  → every row: mountHostIsBody true, appLayoutParent "body", bodyAttrs 'class="relative" id="app" data-paper-field=""', groundState null. Then read index.html:205-213 (mount), :222-226 (data-paper-field rationale), :180-200 (prepaint precedence) against boot/hydrate.ts:53-78 (the second precedence engine).

**Proposed cure.** Take MT-F012's cure and finish it. Move the 8 lines to main.ts referenced via `src=`, with `<div id="app">` as the host. Then: `.app-layout` becomes the app's own root and already declares position:relative, so `class="relative"` is DELETED not moved; `data-paper-field` moves onto `.app-layout` — the element App.vue owns and documents; `<body>` regains the right to carry §6.2's static boot-error region and a `<noscript>`; and main.ts becomes the single reader of the frozen `window.__VALUE_GROUND_BOOT__`, handing it to `createApp(App, { boot })` so App.vue CONSUMES the boot object as §6.2 requires and `resolveHydratedBootModel`'s duplicate precedence engine is deleted outright rather than kept in sync. Necessary but insufficient: it does not fix the 3-root fragment, D-2, D-3 or D-4.

### `DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D) — demo/color-picker/App.vue, the app sh` · D-11 · DESIGN (CHALLENGE-D)

**Defect.** "Not found" has no designed state: an unknown route silently redirects to `/` with no announced reason, rendering byte-identical content to the home route. The canon requires the redirect reason in one polite status plus the destination title/H1.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/color-picker/router/index.ts:37 `{ path: "/:pathMatch(.*)*", redirect: "/" }`. Measured in the tracked matrix: REPORT.md:133 `/#/does-not-exist` text=859 vs REPORT.md:119 `/#/` text=859 — identical, in all four matrices (REPORT.md:133,148,163,178). Canon: VISUAL-CONSTITUTION.md:113 (§5.1) "auth, not-found, or policy redirect | destination H1 | top | redirect reason in one polite status, then destination title/H1; no focus on removed content." The shell mounts no polite status region — its only live region is ErrorBoundary's role="alert" / aria-live="assertive" (ErrorBoundary.vue:6,20), which is assertive and reserved for render throws — and there is no H1 to focus (D-4).
```

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-4 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The card's primary action — expand — is keyboard-inoperable. `role="article"` div with `@click`, no `tabindex`, no `@keydown`, no alternative affordance; the only focusable descendant is the "Palette menu" button. Compounding: `v-bind="press.handlers"` binds `useLiquidPress`'s `onKeydown`/`onKeyup`/`onBlur` to an element that can never be focused — three of eight bound handlers are structurally dead.

**Mechanism.** click-on-a-div as the primary affordance: the container correctly avoids `role="button"` (it houses nested controls) but never provides the named interactive child that should carry the action, so the whole expanded region is gated behind a control keyboard users cannot reach

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/PaletteCard.vue:5-27 (div role=article, v-bind press.handlers, @click emit) · PalettesPane.vue:91 / BrowsePane.vue:102 wire that click to `toggleExpand` · live measurement across 3 cards: {"tabIndex":-1,"cardIsFocusable":false,"focusableDescendants":1,"focusableNames":["Palette menu"]} · node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/useLiquidPress-BOxuDkKa.js handlers block `b = (e) => e.key === "Enter" || e.key === " "` with onKeydown/onKeyup/onBlur
```

**Proposed cure.** Give the action a name and an element: make the palette title a real `<button>` that emits `click` (it is already the semantic label of the card and already carries a click handler for rename), leaving the container a plain `article` whose click stays a mouse-only convenience. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on `demo/palettes/b` · C-5 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** `ActionFeedback` never re-arms its dismissal timer and never clears it on unmount. Because `showFeedback` sets an already-true `visible` ref, the watcher does not fire and the new message inherits the previous message's remaining countdown; and no `onUnmounted` cleanup exists, so a pending timeout fires into a destroyed component and writes to a dead card's state.

**Mechanism.** watching a boolean edge to drive a timer whose identity is really the MESSAGE, plus a raw module-scope `setTimeout` handle with no lifecycle cleanup

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/PaletteCard/ActionFeedback.vue:37-47 (`watch(() => props.visible, …)`) · PaletteCard.vue:238-242 `showFeedback` sets `feedbackVisible.value = true` (no-op when already true) · BrowsePane.vue:226-265 fires showFeedback from 4 async paths against the same card · executable vitest probe (@vue/test-utils + fake timers, host mirrors PaletteCard.vue:123-128), both tests PASS: "visible 100ms after 2nd message: false" (promised 2500ms, delivered 100ms) and "timers pending before unmount: 1 after unmount: 1"
```

**Reproduction.** `npx vitest run --config <probe cfg>` on a mount of ActionFeedback via a host replicating PaletteCard's wiring: showFeedback('Saved!','success'); advanceTimersByTime(2400); showFeedback('Delete failed','error'); advanceTimersByTime(100) → visible === false. Second test: showFeedback then unmount() → vi.getTimerCount() still 1.

**Proposed cure.** The component is a timed toast, so the boolean is the wrong subject: watch message identity (`() => [props.visible, props.message]`) and register `onUnmounted(() => clearTimeout(timer))`. Better still, hoist the dismissal to the caller and let ActionFeedback be pure presentation — that also removes the `update:visible` round-trip back into the parent.
