### `L — library structure (module boundaries, ownership, directi` · L-r2-8 · L

**Defect.** value.js is failure-explicit by design but publishes no unwrap: no subpath exports ok/err or an unwrap helper, only the Result type. The demo hand-rolls the unwrap-or-throw 17 times, twice as the same function five files apart.

**Mechanism.** A library published the discipline (explicit Result) and withheld the ergonomic, so seventeen consumers re-invented the escape hatch, each with its own message format and none with a shared type.

**Evidence.**

```
`cat src/foundation/result.ts` → exports only `Result`, `ok`, `err`; src/subpaths/color.ts:9 exports the Result TYPE alone; no subpath exports an unwrap. `grep -rn "throw new Error(\`" demo --include='*.ts' --include='*.vue' | grep -i error.code` → 17 sites (useGradientCSS.ts ×3, useGradientInterpolation.ts:37, easingCatalogue.ts:103, mixStage.ts:106, useMarkdownColors.ts ×2, generate-color.ts ×3, color-utils.ts:18, ink.ts ×4, palettes/mix.ts:36). Five are in this component's own chain. useGradientCSS.ts:71-77 and easingCatalogue.ts:98-104 are the SAME function, differing only in the error prefix; both are typed `ReturnType<typeof CubicBezier>` while also fed steppedEase results, which type-checks only by coincidence of shape.
```

**Reproduction.** The grep above returns 17 hand-rolled sites; `diff` the two easingValue bodies (useGradientCSS.ts:71-77, easingCatalogue.ts:98-104) — identical but for the string literal.

**Proposed cure.** Publish the unwrap from the foundation as an eighth subpath: `export function unwrap<T, E extends {code: string}>(r: Result<T,E>, context: string): T { if (r.ok) return r.value; throw new Error(`${context}: ${r.error.code}`); }`. Seventeen hand-rolled sites collapse to seventeen call sites of one function with one message grammar, and easingValue stops existing twice.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/color-picke` · C-7 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Every boot rewrites the address bar with a colour the user never picked, violating the hydrate.ts 'born hydrated, ONE commit' law App.vue's own comment asserts.

**Mechanism.** An identity-changing write performed for a value-level clamp, observed by an identity-based watcher — the boot commits a URL write no user action requested.

**Evidence.**

```
Clean browser context (empty localStorage) loading http://localhost:9000/#/generate settles at http://localhost:9000/#/generate?space=lab&color=lab(92%25+88.8+20+/+82.7%25) — measured in every isolated probe run. Mechanism code: useColorPipeline.ts:50-52 unconditionally re-assigns model.value at setup (clampColorToSpaceDomain returns a fresh object; the `if (model.value.color)` guard is always true), tripping the identity-based watcher at useColorUrl.ts:79-82 → router.replace. App.vue:245 then :377 fix the composition order; App.vue:369-376 claims the opposite ('an idempotent re-commit').
```

**Reproduction.** node <scratchpad>/probe-app.mjs (fresh context per run) — read `location.href` after load; it always carries ?space=&color= even with empty storage and a bare hash.

**Proposed cure.** Make the boot clamp a no-op write: compare the clamped colour to the incoming one and skip the assignment when nothing changed (or clamp inside hydrate before the ref exists, which is where the ordering law already says the first value is decided).

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-25 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Non-concentric corner: the full-bleed colour strip carries the card's OUTER 16px radius while sitting at the border's INNER edge, where 14px is required. Together with three stacked zero-blur casters this is the mechanism behind the owner's own mark, which the prior seat's report never references.

**Mechanism.** Clip responsibility was moved onto the child (to avoid 1-bit rasterization at compositing-layer bounds) without moving the radius arithmetic with it. Three copies of a 16px arc at three offsets diverge maximally at the rounds and converge along the straight edges, so the cast reads clean on the sides and faceted/stepped at the corners.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live: card `border-top-left-radius: 16px`, `border-top-width: 2px`, strip inset from card left = `2px` (i.e. exactly at the inner edge), strip `border-top-left-radius: 16px`. Concentric requirement = 16 − 2 = **14px**. Owner artifact: `docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/owner-marked/OM-2-card-shadow-sharp-corners.png`. Shadow half, computed: `oklab(0.28 …/0.32) -3px 3px 0px 0px, oklab(0.28 …/0.26) -5px 5px 0px 0px, oklab(0.28 …/0.18) -7px 7px 0px 0px` — three hard copies, zero blur, zero spread. Radius applied at PaletteCard.vue:36 (`rounded-t-card`), forced by the deliberate refusal of overflow-hidden at :16-18.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes with any populated palette; read `border-top-left-radius`/`border-top-width` on `[role="article"]` and `border-top-left-radius` + `getBoundingClientRect().left` delta on its strip child. Visual: owner-marked/OM-2-card-shadow-sharp-corners.png.

**Proposed cure.** The concentric arithmetic should never be authored by hand. Cure step 1 (`<Card … :shadow="false">`) removes the three casters and therefore the visible artefact; the strip radius then belongs to a producer-side inner-radius token (`calc(var(--radius-card) - var(--card-border-width))`) rather than a repeated `rounded-t-card` literal at the consumer.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-26 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** In dark mode the cel shadow is effectively the same luminance as the surface casting it, and the alpha was raised to compensate rather than the contrast fixed.

**Mechanism.** A hard-edged cel shadow requires luminance headroom beneath the surface; a dark card has none, so the register degrades to a grey smear whose only surviving signal is the offset silhouette. The alpha bump from .32 to .46 is evidence someone noticed the weak read and compensated with opacity instead of contrast.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured on the same element, light vs `.dark`: card `background-color` `oklab(0.913 …)` → `oklab(0.345 …)`; shadow colour `oklab(0.28 …)` → `oklab(0.34 …)`; alphas .32/.26/.18 → **.46/.38/.26**. L(shadow) − L(card) = **−0.633 light** vs **−0.005 dark**. Token: `--shadow-cartoon-md` uses `light-dark(hsl(24 10% 10%), hsl(30 14% 90%))` then `clamp(0.28, l, 0.34)`, so the dark arm takes the LIGHT source colour and clamps it down to 0.34 — landing on the card's own 0.345.
```

**Reproduction.** http://localhost:9000/#/palettes; read `boxShadow` and `backgroundColor` on `[role="article"]`, then `document.documentElement.classList.add('dark')` and read both again.

**Proposed cure.** Not a token patch — the ruled tuple already says `shadow: false` for this species (VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §3.1). Cure step 1 removes the caster entirely; a matte specimen slip needs no cast shadow on either scheme. If any producer follow-up is warranted it is a letter to glass-ui that `--shadow-cartoon-md`'s dark arm clamps into its own surface band.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-27 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The identity row has no overflow design in any direction: once the title is starved to 0 (D-2), the remaining `shrink-0` content exits the card box and then the viewport. The prior seat measured a 37px chip↔menu overlap; the mechanism is unbounded.

**Mechanism.** Title absorbs 100% of negative free space (line-clamp's overflow:hidden zeroes its automatic minimum), reaches 0, and the remaining unshrinkable content simply overflows. `REPORT.md`'s `horizontalOverflow: 0` misses it because an ancestor clips before the document scroll width grows — the content is lost, not merely off-screen.

Measured at 390px viewport, card 324px wide (right edge ≈ 357px), fixture palette with 5 tags: menu button left 307.0 right 343.0; chip 'blue' left 314.9 right 348.7 → **overlapMenuPx: 28.1**; chip 'cool' left 356.7 right 389.9 (outside the card); chip 'ocean' left 397.9 right 441.3 → **84px outside the card, past the 390px viewport**. `metaCluster.scrollWidth − clientWidth = 142`; `row.scrollWidth − clientWidth = 86`. Row structure: PaletteCard.vue:43-79 (`flex items-center justify-between gap-2 min-w-0`) with 9 `shrink-0` siblings, title at :54-59 carrying none.
```

**Reproduction.** Seed a palette with `tier:'featured'`, 5 tags, forkCount/versionCount, and a long name; load http://localhost:9000/#/palettes at 390×844; read the chip rects against the card's right edge.

**Proposed cure.** Structural, per the ruled anatomy: the identity line gets its own row with `flex-1 min-w-0` and the meta cluster is demoted below it or behind a single count — the chips stop being peers of the title. This is the same move that cures D-2, D-5 and D-18, and it is why `PaletteCardMeta` must not exist as a bare multi-root fragment of `shrink-0` siblings spliced into the parent's flex row. Note the `.slice(0, 3)` tag cap is not conservative truncation — it is the only thing bounding this escape, and three tags already escape.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-21 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** useHeightTransition's onAfterEnter calls scrollIntoView({behavior:"smooth"}), which by spec bypasses the app's global prefers-reduced-motion guard: every card expansion smooth-scrolls the page for a user who asked for reduced motion.

**Mechanism.** A height-morph composable that also performs document navigation — two unrelated responsibilities in one seam, and the second one escapes the CSS-level motion policy.

**Evidence.**

```
demo/palettes/browser/card/composables/useHeightTransition.ts:48 — `htmlEl.scrollIntoView({ behavior: "smooth", block: "nearest" });`. The guard at demo/styles/animations.css:184-192 sets `scroll-behavior: auto !important` on `*`. CSSOM-View defers to the CSS scroll-behavior property only when the `behavior` option is "auto"; an explicit "smooth" forces a smooth scroll regardless. (The same composable's inline `style.transition` writes ARE caught, by the !important duration override — so the guard works everywhere except where JS overrides it explicitly.)
```

**Reproduction.** Deterministic from the spec + source: enable prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, expand a palette card whose body is off-screen; the page scrolls smoothly. No probe run.

**Proposed cure.** Scroll-into-view is the pane's decision, not the transition's — hoist it out of the composable. If it stays, read the motion preference and pass behavior: prm ? "auto" : "smooth".

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-13 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The mobile headline wraps to a 27%-filled orphan line — a three-term tuple broken 2+1, the worst available break.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured at 390x844: last painted line of .readout carries 88.7px of ink in a 327.7px box = 27.1% filled, 72.9% void. PROPORTION-AUDIT §2.5 permits a second line only for "a tuple whose rendered legal width actually wraps" but is silent on where the break falls.
```

**Reproduction.** At 390x844 on the settled / route, take Range.getClientRects() over .readout, group by rounded top, sum the widths of the rects on the last line (88.7px) and compare with .readout getBoundingClientRect().width (327.7px).

**Proposed cure.** Give the tuple an explicit break policy in the composition — all-on-one-line (via the paired clamp of D-05 sized to the guaranteed capacity) or an even 1+1+1 stack — rather than greedy fill. The break is a design decision and must be authored, not inherited from flex-wrap.

**Proposed cure.** Delete initialParse. Its job — don't flash red at a user who has not typed yet — is already done correctly by the callers: the boot paths that seed the model no longer go through parseAndSetColor at all (hydrate.ts), and the one that does (restoreFromStorage) is restoring a value the user themselves last committed. A latch that survives boot to eat a real error is a masking fallback (edict 2).

**Defect.** `findCustomName` is an O(n) linear scan of a Map keyed the wrong way round, called by three hot computeds and once per palette swatch.

**Evidence.**

```
useCustomColorNames.ts:61-66 walks normalizedCustomNames (name -> xyz) comparing values. Callers: formattedCurrentColor, currentColorMeta, canProposeName (three scans per invalidation) and savedColorLabel at useColorNameResolution.ts:48-53 (once per saved swatch). getApprovedColorNames accepts limit up to 500 (api/src/modules/color/schema.ts:27) and the demo passes none (color-names.ts:23-31), so the registry is server-sized. Verified live: findCustomName(xyz) = "babb-blue".
```

**Reproduction.** Same harness, test E in roundtrip.probe.ts. Not currently hot only because R3-3's 100 ms debounce caps invalidations at ~10/s — fixing R3-3 as prescribed removes that accidental cap, so the two must be repaired together.

**Proposed cure.** Build the inverse index (xyz -> name) inside the same loop that builds normalizedCustomNames at useCustomColorNames.ts:20-33. One extra Map.set, O(1) lookups, and the collision case of R3-2 becomes visible at registry-build time — which is where it wants to be caught.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D-14 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** Direction and bidi: every offset is physical, and the field renders a CSS-colour string with no LTR isolation.

**Mechanism.** Physical-axis geometry plus an un-isolated LTR technical value inside a container that may be RTL — under RTL a value beginning with `#` or `/` reorders on screen while the model keeps the original bytes, so what the user reads is not what the parser receives.

**Evidence.**

```
ColorInput.vue physical offsets: `pr-9` (:18), `right-2` (:35), `.send-btn { right: 0.25rem }` (:337), `.error-badge { right: 0.5rem }` (:350), `mask-image: linear-gradient(to right, …)` (:300). No `dir` attribute and no `unicode-bidi: isolate` on the value (measured attribute list: data-v-…, contenteditable, role, aria-label, class). Combined with measured `textAlign: center`. VISUAL-CONSTITUTION §6.1: 'chrome, navigation and layout — logical inline/block direction follows the document' and 'CSS strings, hex, slugs, IDs and provenance — render in LTR-isolated spans inside RTL prose.'
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — hypothesis for the visual reordering (no RTL locale is currently reachable in-app). The physical-offset inventory and the absence of any dir/unicode-bidi attribute are directly verified from source and from the live attribute enumeration.

**Proposed cure.** Logical properties throughout (`pe-9`, `inset-inline-end`), and `dir="ltr"` on the value element — which glass-ui `Input` makes trivial. Drop `text-align: center` for inline-start alignment; a technical LTR value centred in a possibly-RTL container is the worst of both.

Everything else in the dock is transform/opacity only: vj-settle = scale(1)→1.03→1 at demo/styles/animations.css:170. ### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / owners` · L-21 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The document heading outline is inverted, not merely missing an h1: the page's most prominent title is an H3 whose own subsections are H2s. No module owns heading level.

**Evidence.**

```
h1 = 0 on 60/60 captures (docs/tranches/V/megatranche/audit/visual/REPORT.md per-capture table) and live. Live outline (scratchpad L-probe.mjs, /#/, 1280x900, document order): ['H3:92.0%,88.8,20.0', 'H3:About the color spaces, La', 'H2:Basic Information', 'H2:Components', 'H2:Key Properties', 'H2:Conversion Graph', 'H2:Usage', 'H2:Detailed Guide', 'H3:Attributes', 'H3:Historical Context']. `grep -rn '<h1' demo --include=*.vue | wc -l` -> 0. The datum exists in the right place with exactly one consumer: demo/shell/viewSchema.ts:104-233 `label` per view, read only by demo/color-picker/router/useDocumentTitle.ts:47-56 (`composeTitle`).
```

**Reproduction.** node scratchpad/L-probe.mjs — reads document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3,...') in order on the live picker route. A screen-reader outline reads: (no title) -> level 3 'About the color spaces' -> level 2 'Basic Information' — the child outranks its parent.

**Proposed cure.** Extend the existing owner rather than adding one: `useDocumentTitle` becomes `useDocumentIdentity(route)` returning `{ title, heading }` from the same `viewSchema` row, the shell renders `<h1 class="sr-only">{{ heading }}</h1>` as the first child of App.vue's `<main>`, and panes start at `h2` by rule. ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation (assume the component is improp` · D-9 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** devicePixelRatio is ignored — the loupe canvas backing store is a hardcoded 110×110 regardless of DPR, so the deliberately crisp (imageSmoothingEnabled=false) pixel grid is bilinearly upsampled by the compositor. LOUPE_SIZE also has two sources of truth: the constant drives the CSS and the draw math, but the canvas attributes are literals.

**Mechanism.** fixed-pixel backing store on a device-pixel-scaled display; duplicated dimension constant

**Evidence.**

```
ImageEyedropper.vue:85 (`width="110" height="110"` literals); constants.ts:8 (LOUPE_SIZE = 110) used at ImageEyedropper.vue:191-196 and useLoupeCanvas.ts:35-51; useLoupeCanvas.ts:40 (imageSmoothingEnabled = false). `grep -n "devicePixelRatio|dpr"` over the ImageEyedropper directory → no matches. ```

**Reproduction.** Open the eyedropper on any retina display (probe measured devicePixelRatio: 2) and inspect the loupe canvas: backing 110×110, CSS box 106 px, 212 device px. The magnified pixel edges are smeared by the compositor.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt on demo/workbenches` · C7 · CHALLENGE-C

The ramp's own sample step is 3.13% (`oklch(0.75 0.15 145) 0%` → `oklch(0.746875 0.150937 148.75) 3.13%`), so the ghost fill vs the pixel beneath it differ by ≈2.9° of hue near the terminals. **Proposed cure.** One polite live region per bench, owned by the editor root, fed by the EXISTING copyStatus: success → "Copied <literal>", failure → "Copy failed — clipboard unavailable". ### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects in demo/workbenches/gra` · C8 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Dual write path for the selection plus an unbound public model; and the defineModel stale-read hazard is ARMED (pass-1's mechanism justification was wrong)

**Mechanism.** The parent DOES bind v-model:selected-id, so a write to selectedId.value is invisible to a subsequent read until the parent's ref updates, the parent re-renders and the prop reaches the child's watchSyncEffect — exactly the repo-recorded hazard standing law #7 prescribes a local shallowRef for. No current call site reads after write in the same tick (wasSelected at :123 is captured before the write at :129), so the verdict is a checked negative — but by luck of ordering, not by a synchronous model, and selectedId is written from four sites (:129,:152,:160,:178).

**Evidence.**

```
GradientStopEditor.vue:129-130 writes selectedId AND emits 'select'; GradientVisualizer.vue:140,144 wires both; grep for selectedStopId finds only 3 lines and GradientPane.vue never binds it. Mechanism correction from node_modules/@vue/runtime-core/dist/runtime-core.cjs.js:4321-4332 (vue 3.5.35, verified via require('vue/package.json').version): `localValue = value` runs ONLY when the parent has NOT passed v-model.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — latent hazard, plus a source-level dual path. Read the Vue useModel setter and the two parent bindings.

**Proposed cure.** Make selection a plain local ref in the stop editor, delete the 'select' emit and its handler, and delete GradientVisualizer's unbound selectedStopId defineModel. That removes the dual path, the dead public surface, and the armed stale-read in one move.

GradientStopEditor.vue:30-33 and :255-261 document the defect in prose; hoveredId ref at :33, handleScale at :60-63, @pointerenter/@pointerleave on every handle at :269-270, transform+transition re-authored per instance at :262-263.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defects (SearchFilterBar.vue, a` · C-11 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** The filter popover can neither shrink nor scroll: max-height is none, overflow-y is visible, and there is no floating-ui `size` middleware — so once the tag list and the Clear-all row are present the content is projected to exceed a phone viewport with no way to reach the bottom.

**Mechanism.** popover sized by content with collision handling that can shift but not resize — no size middleware, no max-height, no inner scroll container on the content root

**Evidence.**

```
Measured live at 390x664 with the tag section absent: dialog height 441.5px; on the popover root `overflowY: "visible"`, `maxHeight: "none"`, `scrollHeight: 439` === `clientHeight: 439` (no inner scroll). Arithmetic: the tag block adds max-h-28 = 112px plus its section label and padding (~43px) and the Clear-all row adds ~44px -> ~640px against a 664px viewport.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — labelled a HYPOTHESIS. Not reproduced because the live tag catalog is empty (`curl -s https://api.color.babb.dev/colors/tags` -> `[]`), so the tag block never renders. Separately I observed one transient 81.5px bottom overflow (dialog y=304, height 441.5, bottom 745.5 vs viewport 664) which floating-ui's collision shift then resolved to a fitting position — that transient is NOT reported as a defect.

**Proposed cure.** Give the popover content a `max-height: var(--reka-popover-content-available-height)` with `overflow-y: auto` on the content root (root-level, in the glass-ui PopoverContent variant rather than as a per-instance override), so the panel scrolls instead of clipping regardless of tag count.

**Defect.** `ActionBarToggle`'s `slotLive` early return makes the watch's re-arm dead code: on a later false->true edge `settled` is never restored by the watch, and the invariant the O-15b oracle asserts is held only by an unacknowledged `transitionend` side channel.

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · D2-12 · CHALLENGE-D

### `CHALLENGE-D — design (visual truth, state coverage, motion, ` · R3-12 · CHALLENGE-D

**Defect.** The demo's global reduced-motion transition guard is inert app-wide; the producer's rule wins, so this component's PRM behaviour is accidental rather than designed.

**Mechanism.** A `*`-selector `!important` guard in consumer CSS outranked by a producer `!important` rule at higher specificity — so the consumer's declared PRM policy for transitions has no effect anywhere in the app.

**Evidence.**

```
Measured under `reducedMotion: "reduce"`, frames/r3probe3.json: `transitionDuration: "0.1s"`, `animationDuration: "1e-05s"`, with matching rules `{sel: ":not([data-allow-motion])", media: "(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)", td: "0.1s", imp: "important"}` (glass-ui, specificity 0,1,0) and `{sel: "*, ::before, ::after", td: "0.01ms", imp: "important"}` (demo/styles/animations.css:184-193, specificity 0,0,0). The producer rule wins. This CORRECTS round-2 section 5, which credited compliance to the demo guard.
```

**Reproduction.** Launch with `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, open the field, read `getComputedStyle(el).transitionDuration` — 0.1 s, not the 0.01 ms the demo guard declares. Animations still resolve to 1e-05s, so the guard is live for `animation-duration` only.

**Proposed cure.** Delete the consumer's blanket transition arm and defer to the producer's PRM register, or raise the guard's specificity deliberately — but do not ship a rule the codebase believes is authoritative and is not. (Outcome here is benign: a 100 ms colour transition is appropriate under reduced motion.)

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure / module boundaries / owners` · L-22 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The demo's declared view of the published library surface has drifted from `package.json#exports`: tsconfig.demo.json maps a nonexistent `dist/index.d.ts`, declares two subpaths that are not exported, and omits two that are — while calling itself a mirror of the generated Vite alias set.

**Mechanism.** A hand-maintained declaration of a generated surface: the runtime alias set is derived from exports, the type paths are not, so the two views of the public API drift silently.

**Evidence.**

```
`package.json#exports` keys = ['./color','./value','./css','./easing','./math','./transform','./quantize'] — 7 keys, no '.' root. tsconfig.demo.json paths declare `@mkbabb/value.js` -> ./dist/index.d.ts (`ls dist/index*` -> no matches found), plus `/parsing` and `/units` (neither in exports; no src/subpaths/parsing.ts or units.ts — `ls src/subpaths` -> color, css, easing, math, quantize, transform, value), and omit `/value` and `/css` (both exported; `/css` used 10x in demo and 4x inside glass-ui's dist). The file's header calls this 'the 8 public keys' / 'a CLOSED 8-key set' that 'mirrors the vite.config.ts runtime self-alias generated from the same map'; vite.config.ts:41-50 generates one alias per exports entry -> 7 aliases and no bare-root alias.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — latent, not live. No demo file imports the bare `@mkbabb/value.js` specifier (`grep -rn '@mkbabb/value.js"' demo` -> the only hit is prose at demo/shared/utils.ts:12), and glass-ui's three specifiers (/color, /css, /easing, measured in its dist) are all covered by the generated alias set, so one instance serves the running app. Were the bare specifier ever written it would resolve to node_modules/@mkbabb/value.js@4.0.0 — the published copy npm installed for glass-ui's peer dep — a second instance of this library behind an undeclared specifier.

**Proposed cure.** Generate the tsconfig `paths` from `package.json#exports` exactly as the Vite aliases already are (one loader, one source of truth), or add a real `"."` export plus `dist/index.d.ts`. Either way the two declarations of the public surface cannot drift apart again — this is the axis T.W1's dogfood keystone was fought over.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation audit of demo/workbenches/gener` · C-18 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** WatercolorDot reads its `seed` prop once at setup, so the consumer's colour-derived `:seed="gen-${css}-${i}"` only ever applies its mount-time value — the 'seeded stable per (color,i)' claim decays after the first regenerate.

**Mechanism.** A by-value option passed to a composable that treats it as static, while the consumer passes a value it expects to be reactive. Family: NON-REACTIVE-OPTION-READ-ONCE.

**Evidence.**

```
GenerateControls.vue:196 comment 'seeded stable per (color,i)'; :204 :seed binding. node_modules/@mkbabb/glass-ui/dist/watercolor-dot.js: useWatercolorBlob destructures `{ …, seed: c = "" }` once from the options object, and its colour watcher recomputes `hashString(newColor + c)` using that closed-over mount-time `c`; only the feTurbulence seed is a computed on (color + seed). The two halves of one dot therefore disagree about their seed after a regenerate.
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — I did not capture a before/after silhouette diff, and the dots are unreachable for interaction anyway (C-1). Labelled a hypothesis on the observable effect; the code path itself is quoted above and is not in doubt.

**Proposed cure.** Consumer side (BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8): pass a stable `gen-${i}` seed, since a colour-derived seed is a category error against that contract and buys nothing. Producer side (relay, optional): make useWatercolorBlob take seed as a getter/ref so the silhouette and the wet edge stay in agreement.

The two buttons are 6px apart (gap-1.5), so the SC 2.5.8 spacing exception would not rescue them if the size shrank. For contrast, the specimen tiles measure 45.2×43.8 and 44.0×43.8 — comfortably clear.

**Reproduction.** open /#/gradient and run `[...document.querySelectorAll('.rail-btn')].map(e=>{const r=e.getBoundingClientRect();return {w:r.width,h:r.height,label:e.getAttribute('aria-label')}})` → both 24×24.

### `CHALLENGE-C — implementation defect hunt: demo/workbenches/g` · C-12 · CHALLENGE-C

**Defect.** Module-level easing resolution cache with no eviction and no size cap.

**Mechanism.** unbounded-cache: a memo keyed on unbounded user input with no eviction policy.

```
useGradientCSS.ts:69 `const resolvedEasingCache = new Map<string, EasingFunction>();` — populated at :131, never cleared. Reached only for literal-only intervals (easingFnOf short-circuits on interval.fn at :122, which authored intervals always carry), so growth is bounded by the number of distinct easing literals ever parsed from pasted CSS. ```

GenerateControls.vue:75-81 — `preset.value = value as PresetName;` / `harmony.value = value as HarmonyName;` · node_modules/reka-ui/dist/index3.d.cts:231 — `type AcceptableValue = string | number | bigint | Record<string, any> | null` · demo/color-session/generate-color.ts:220 `const p = GENERATION_PRESETS[preset];` then :227 `p.l[0] + rng() * (p.l[1] - p.l[0])`
```

**Reproduction.** NONE — this is a HYPOTHESIS. I found no path in the shipped UI that makes reka emit null here (no clear affordance is wired to either Select). The mechanism is certain; the trigger is unreached.

**Proposed cure.** Replace the cast with a membership check against the arrays that already exist — `if (!PRESET_NAMES.includes(value as PresetName)) return;` — so the boundary validates rather than asserts.

### `CHALLENGE-L — library structure (module boundaries, ownershi` · L-9 · CHALLENGE-L

**Defect.** The dropdown preview-strip cost claim holds at the default count but fails by 2.8× at the maximum; the strips are plain template function calls (never memoized), and the chip module's segment budget is private so the host over-generates.

**Mechanism.** Asymmetric module surface: the ramp chip publishes its sampling budget so hosts can size their work, the strip chip hides its cap — so at count>7 the host pays to generate stops the renderer discards. Compounded by the absence of memoization: every re-render of the mounted SelectContent recomputes all 16 strips.

**Evidence.**

```
Claim at GenerateControls.vue:88-93: "10 rows × 5-12 library generations is sub-millisecond". Measured (node/V8, bundled core): one generatePalette count=5 = 0.097 ms; count=12 = 0.362 ms; 10 preset strips @count=5 = 0.871 ms (claim HOLDS); 6 harmony strips @count=5 = 0.699 ms; 10 preset strips @count=12 = 2.80 ms (claim FAILS 2.8×). presetStops/harmonyStops at :94-100 are plain functions called from the template. STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP=7 is a private const in demo/color-session/color-chips/PreviewStrip.vue while the sibling RAMP form exports RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT from color-chips/sample.ts and its barrel.
```

**Reproduction.** esbuild-bundle demo/color-session/generate-color.ts, then bench 10× generatePalette per preset at count 5 and 12 — 0.871 ms and 2.80 ms respectively over 500 iterations after warmup.

**Proposed cure.** Export STRIP_SEGMENT_CAP from the color-chips barrel (symmetry with RAMP_SAMPLE_COUNT) and wrap the two truth functions in computeds keyed on (count, preset, harmony, seed). NOT 'generate only 7' — generateHues derives its step from count for the analogous harmony, so a 7-generation is not the prefix of a 12-generation and truncating would break the seed-exactness law. BLOCKED-ON-GLASS-V8 for this file.
